source:
a game. so the lobby is a screen loader as there's 3 buttons. "PLAY" "GAME PASSES" "SKINS" the skins are avatar skins. when u press the play button you'll be taken to an area that says "create lobby" and "join lobby" when u press create lobby you'll have the player count. the max is 5. you have story mode and endless mode. the modes with be explained shortly. okay so when your friends join in. there will be a button that says start. u press it

(Story mode) 

you load in and a text appears on your screen "you just got offered to stay in a mall for a week for 500,000 dollars. do u accept?" there will be a yes or no option. if u press yes u get loaded in. if u press no then that option goes and the only option is yes. forcing u to pick yes. u load in to find yourself by the entrance of the mall. u enter and u find yourself by the door with a mall like map. a paper on ground and when u press it it says: "rules: no leaving. no looking out the windows on the third floor at midnight." there will be an x button u press to exit it. u explore the area and there's a text up top. it'll say day one. when u explore after u finish u have to go to a furniture store to sleep in. it's in the second floor. u go upstairs and sleep. it's day two. u explore. and go to restaurants to eat food. and play around. u go to sleep in the same furniture store and it skips to five days. thats when weird stuff starts happening. for example u go to restaurants to eat but u see dirty dishes on the counter top u definitely haven't Aten. messes u didn't create. and other paranormal things.

answers.ask: How big should the mall read - a small two-anchor mall you can cross in 20 seconds, or a sprawling superregional one?
answers.answer: Make it a small two-anchor mall that players can cross in about 20 seconds, with the entrance, furniture store, restaurants, and third floor clearly accessible.

answers.ask: Does the week end in an escape, a death, or just a last day? Story mode has no stated win condition.
answers.answer: The week ends with a last day; the prompt does not call for an escape or death ending.

answers.ask: What is Endless mode - the same mall on repeat, or a different space entirely?
answers.answer: Endless mode is the same mall on repeat, with paranormal events continuing as long as the lobby survives.

## Clarifications resolved
- [author] scale — Q: How big should the mall read - a small two-anchor mall you can cross in 20 seconds, or a sprawling superregional one? A: Make it a small two-anchor mall that players can cross in about 20 seconds, with the entrance, furniture store, restaurants, and third floor clearly accessible.
- [author] goal — Q: Does the week end in an escape, a death, or just a last day? Story mode has no stated win condition. A: The week ends with a last day; the prompt does not call for an escape or death ending.
- [author] genre — Q: What is Endless mode - the same mall on repeat, or a different space entirely? A: Endless mode is the same mall on repeat, with paranormal events continuing as long as the lobby survives.
- [agent_inferred] restaurant_count — Q: How many restaurants should the compact mall include? A: Two small restaurants sharing one ground-floor dining area.
- [agent_inferred] spawn_position — Q: Is a separate exterior needed before entering the mall? A: No; start inside the entrance vestibule so the three-floor mall is the complete map.

## Enriched image prompt
Create one compact three-floor mall interior that players can cross in about 20 seconds. Start in a ground-floor entrance vestibule with a paper lying beside the inner door. Arrange two small restaurants around one shared dining area on the ground floor. Place the furniture-store anchor on the second floor, with bed displays that can serve as the group’s sleep area. Keep the third floor clearly accessible by a central stair and give it prominent windows overlooking the interior and outside darkness. Use a readable central atrium so all floors stay oriented.

Build clean normal and progressively paranormal dressing states on the same layout: later states add unexplained dirty dishes, displaced objects, messes, and subtle architectural oddities without changing the core circulation. Story and Endless modes reuse this mall; loading screens, lobby creation, player count, buttons, dialogue choices, day text, and mode selection are UI or mechanics rather than separate physical spaces.

## Genre
The dominant genre is Adventure because story-driven exploration of the mall leads the experience, with Survival secondary for the repeating paranormal Endless mode.

## Shape and preset
Use `interior-single`, a Zone (Single Interior), because the whole game map is one enclosed mall. No Adventure or Survival preset fits a compact three-floor story mall without inventing exits, monsters, or chapters as separate maps, so the preset is none.

## Config requirements
Use the visible side of `trigger-task` for the second-floor bed displays and two restaurant counters. Use `zone-graphics` for localized paranormal dressing clusters that can intensify without replacing the base map. Add the entrance paper as scene-specific image geometry with no canonical option ID.

## Layout requirements
Place `trigger-task` as three TriggerZones: one sleep zone among the furniture-store beds and one eating zone at each of two restaurant counters. Place one free-text TriggerZone with no canonical ID on the entrance paper for reading its rules.

## Layout components
The mall has three stacked floors, one entrance vestibule, one central atrium, two restaurants and shared dining on floor one, one furniture store on floor two, prominent third-floor windows, and stairs linking every level. Normal and paranormal states share this exact plan.

## Render order
Use `topdown`: make all three floor plans and stair alignments authoritative, then dress normal and paranormal isometric variants.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
The scale band is medium because storefront, paper, counters, beds, and stairs must remain legible in a 20-second mall. The theme is ordinary enclosed retail space turning into restrained paranormal horror. Use `P2` because three walkable floors overhang one another.
